description: Roketçilik, drone teknolojileri, mühendislik ve yazılım alanları çalışan; dahahönce benzer yarışmalara katılmış bir ekibiz. NASA Space Apps Challenge'da bu deneyimimizi uzay ve bilim odaklı gerçek problemlere yaratçı, uygulanabilir çözümler gelişimek için kullanmayı hedefliyoruz.
summary:
AstroApex is a web application built for the NASA Space Apps "Lunar Landing Site Navigator" challenge to optimize landing site and date selection on the Moon. Near the lunar south pole, minor shifts in coordinates or launch delays drastically alter solar power and direct-to-Earth communication.

Users compare two scenarios from 27 preset sites or custom coordinates. Unlike typical static viewers, AstroApex achieves flight-grade precision by integrating real NASA SPICE/DE440 ephemeris data with LRO/LOLA elevation models in JavaScript. Timelines visualize illumination, communication, and co-visibility windows, while an integrated battery model evaluates survival through prolonged darkness.

What sets our project apart is unifying true celestial mechanics, topography, and mission scheduling in one side-by-side comparison. Interactive 3D mapping, site scanning, and rover routing simplify target access, while a built-in assistant recalculates alternatives and PDF/CSV exports streamline collaboration.

Built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Python—alongside a standalone C/Lua/SPICE engine and automated tests—AstroApex features an intuitive dark UI with color-coded indicators and English/Turkish support. Running offline from a single HTML file with zero server dependencies, it empowers engineers to rapidly trade off constraints and helps students grasp lunar mission design.
details:
AstroApex is an offline-capable web platform built for the NASA Space Apps "Lunar Landing Site Navigator" challenge to optimize lunar landing site and date selection. Near the Moon’s south pole, minor coordinate shifts or launch delays drastically alter solar illumination and direct-to-Earth communication.

Users compare two scenarios across 27 preset sites or custom coordinates. Unlike basic viewers, AstroApex achieves flight-grade precision by merging Python-processed NASA SPICE/DE440 ephemeris data with LRO/LOLA elevation models in JavaScript. Timelines track Sun/Earth visibility and co-visibility windows, while an integrated battery model evaluates survival through prolonged darkness.

Our creative innovation unifies celestial mechanics, 3D topography, and mission scheduling in one side-by-side workspace. Interactive 3D terrain mapping, site scanning, and rover traverse routing simplify scientific target access. A built-in assistant recalculates alternatives, while PDF/CSV exports streamline team collaboration.

Developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, and a standalone C/Lua/SPICE engine with automated tests, AstroApex runs from a single server-free HTML file. Balancing terrain resolution, power constraints, communication blackouts, and intuitive bilingual (EN/TR) dark-UI design, it empowers engineers to rapidly evaluate mission trade-offs and helps students grasp lunar exploration design.
